content.value_statement: Dart CLI projects need consistent command routing, error handling, tests, and release steps. This skill provides practical guidance for building and distributing them.
actual_capabilities: Explains Dart CLI project layout with bin, lib/src, and public library files.
Guides argument parsing with ArgParser, CommandRunner, and Command classes.
Covers standard exit codes, error output, and asynchronous stack traces.
Describes integration testing with test_process and test_descriptor.
Shows Dart compilation options for native executables and AOT snapshots.
Lists Linux cross-compilation target flags and release validation steps.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a generated complete application.
It does not install Dart, packages, or build tools.
Cross-compilation guidance is limited to the Dart targets described in the skill.
Application-specific security, packaging, and release policies need separate review.

use_cases.title: Start a command-line tool
use_cases.description: Create a Dart CLI with a conventional directory layout and basic argument parsing.

use_cases.title: Add a subcommand safely
use_cases.description: Plan command routing, validation, help text, error handling, and automated tests.

use_cases.title: Prepare a native release
use_cases.description: Validate, compile, and choose host or Linux cross-compilation targets for distribution.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic CLI
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me structure a new Dart CLI named inventory_tool. Include bin and lib/src responsibilities and basic argument parsing.

prompt_templates.title: Add a subcommand
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add an import subcommand to my Dart CommandRunner. Define its flags, validation, exit behavior, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Write integration tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to test a Dart CLI command with test_process and test_descriptor, including stdout, exit code, and filesystem assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a native release
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release checklist for my Dart CLI. Include formatting, analysis, tests, host compilation, and Linux cross-compilation considerations.

output_examples.input: Add a backup subcommand to a Dart CLI.
output: Suggested CommandRunner registration and argument definitions.
Validation and non-zero exit behavior for invalid input.
A test plan for process output and generated files.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Dart CLI for Linux distribution.
output: A validation sequence for formatting, analysis, and tests.
Host and Linux compilation command guidance.
Notes about target operating system and architecture flags.

best_practices: Keep executable entry points in bin and implementation details in lib/src.
Return descriptive errors to stderr with appropriate non-zero exit codes.
Run formatting, static analysis, and automated tests before compiling releases.
anti_patterns: Do not place all command logic directly in the bin entry point.
Do not swallow exceptions when the command cannot recover safely.
Do not release a compiled executable without validating help text and user flows.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design, test, compile, and distribute Dart command-line applications.

faq.question: Does it create files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for you to apply in your project.

faq.question: Which Dart argument APIs does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers ArgParser for simple scripts and CommandRunner with Command for subcommands.

faq.question: Does it cover CLI testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes process and filesystem integration tests using Dart testing packages.

faq.question: Can it help compile native executables?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains dart compile exe and AOT snapshot workflows.

faq.question: Does it support every operating system target?
faq.answer: No. Follow the Dart SDK documentation for the targets supported by your installed SDK.
